question.text: The temperature of an open room of volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></math> increases from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>17</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>27</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> due to the sunshine. The atmospheric pressure in the room remains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi>Pa</mi></math>. If <math><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math> and <math><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub></math> are the number of molecules in the room before and after heating, then <math><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mrow><mi>n</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></math> will be:

solution.text:
Ti=273+17=290K

Tf=273+27=300K
